title: Ben Johnson on preparing for Packers | Press Conference
headline: Tyson Bagent is set to start again at Lambeau; Johnson wants him to take more downfield shots and promises Odunze, Burden and Loveland earlier touches.
summary: Johnson spent the opening on Green Bay. He praised Jeff Hafley's... no, Gannon's defense for its speed, its safeties and a new Mike linebacker, and called Jordan Love one of the league's most accurate quarterbacks. Much of the session was about Tyson Bagent's second start. Johnson said Bagent handles pre-snap changes well and has a good mix of looks to read, including Arizona-style disguised rotations. He wants Bagent to take the second-level throws he passed up last week and gave him a 'green light.' Johnson put it on himself to get Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland the ball earlier in games. He said D'Andre Swift's two fumbles are very uncharacteristic, and the one last week was 'egregious,' but he expects it to be fixed. Jonah Jackson has graded at or near the top of the offensive line through four weeks. Ozzy Trapilo is getting closer to returning and Theo Benedet played solidly last week. Roster decisions on the three PUP players, including Kyler Gordon, will wait until late in the week. The team is also adjusting practice workload after the offense ran 89 plays while the defense barely played.

injuries.detail: One of three PUP players who could be activated into the open roster spot; the decision will come at the end of the week.
Getting closer each week through padded practices, but no firm timeline was given.

signals.claim: Bagent will start at QB at Green Bay and be encouraged to take more second-level downfield throws.
signals.note: He has the green light to push the ball downfield, which lifts the ceiling for the Bears' receivers.
signals.quote: hey, you get the green light, man.

signals.claim: Odunze will get the ball in his hands earlier in games and see more downfield opportunities.
signals.note: Johnson blamed his own play-calling and promised more early looks for Odunze.
signals.quote: try to get in his hands a little bit earlier in the game

signals.claim: Burden will keep getting more opportunities as the staff works to get the playmakers involved.
signals.note: Johnson said he felt Burden come alive Sunday and wants to keep feeding him.
signals.quote: I felt that from Luther

signals.claim: Loveland should see more chances, though Johnson said only that he showed it 'to a degree.'
signals.note: Johnson was less emphatic about Loveland than about the receivers.
signals.quote: felt that from Colston to a degree as well

signals.claim: Swift will fix his ball security after two fumbles this season.
signals.note: Fumble concerns could affect his workload if they continue, but Johnson expects a quick fix.
signals.quote: I think the one last week was egregious though.

signals.claim: Jackson will keep playing at a top-of-the-line level on the offensive line.
signals.note: A strong interior line supports the run game and pass protection for Bagent.
signals.quote: Jonah's playing high level football right now.

signals.claim: Benedet will keep his role on the offensive line and improve with more experience.
signals.note: He played well in the run game, which keeps him in the mix while Trapilo works back.
signals.quote: he played solid last week and is only going to play better

signals.claim: Trapilo could be ready to play soon but is not confirmed for this week.
signals.note: His return would shake up the offensive line rotation.
signals.quote: he's getting closer and closer each and every week.

signals.claim: The team will decide at the end of the week whether Gordon or another PUP player is activated.
signals.note: A Gordon return would help the secondary against Green Bay's passing game.
signals.quote: make a decision at the end of the week

topics.detail: Johnson praised the speed, the safeties and nickel, and the new Mike linebacker. He expects disguised coverages that show one look and rotate at the snap, similar to Arizona, so route runners and Bagent need discipline.
He called Jordan Love one of the most accurate quarterbacks in the league and said Green Bay's outside speed has given Chicago problems in the past.
Chicago expects to use a silent cadence on the road. Johnson said the staff deliberately made spring and camp chaotic so any quarterback can execute.
The offense ran 89 plays while the defense barely played, so the staff adjusted this week's practice without going to a full walkthrough, while still making sure players are being smart about reps.
Johnson was surprised by the retirement after one game. He said the player had looked good in padded practices, and the team will move on.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Taking Over the Defense & Tank Dell’s Return
headline: Ryans is taking over defensive play-calling from Matt Burke; Tank Dell began practicing, M.J. Stewart is set to play Sunday, and Azeez Al-Shaair is hopeful for the Titans game.
summary: Ryans announced he will take over defensive play-calling this week to streamline communication and spark change after a winless 0-4 start. He said it was no slight against Matt Burke and that the defense is not being overhauled. Tank Dell practiced for the first time in his comeback; Ryans said it was good to see him running routes and that there is no hard timeline. Two other players were also back at practice for the first time (the names are garbled in the captions), and each will progress on his own schedule. M.J. Stewart is healthy and will be ready to go Sunday. A linebacker working on a side field, almost certainly Al-Shaair, the Pro Bowl middle linebacker, is hopeful to return for the game. On offense, Ryans said pass protection has been much better and C.J. Stroud is throwing well. He said the run game needs cleaner finishing and sustained blocks, especially against Jeffery Simmons, because David Montgomery has been getting hit in the backfield. He praised the Titans and his friend Robert Saleh and called the game a must-win for both teams.

injuries.detail: Practiced for the first time in his comeback, running routes and getting plays. No hard timeline; the goal is to acclimate and get into team reps.
Healthy and back to himself after practicing for a couple of weeks. He will be up and ready to go Sunday.
Worked on a side field. Ryans said the team is hopeful to get him back for the game and called him a key piece (the Mike linebacker).
Appears to be one of three players back at practice for the first time (captions say 'Caden MacDonald'). He will be worked back in with reps and progress at his own pace.

signals.claim: Dell will continue ramping up in practice with no set return date or deadline.
signals.note: His practice return is a positive step, but there is no timeline, so he is a stash or watch candidate rather than a startable receiver.
signals.quote: We're not putting a, you know, a hard deadline or set timeline on it.

signals.claim: Al-Shaair may return for the Titans game after working on a side field.
signals.note: He is hopeful rather than confirmed. His status matters for IDP and for the defense's communication.
signals.quote: We're hopeful to get him back for the game.

signals.claim: Stewart will be active and play Sunday against the Titans.
signals.note: A healthy Stewart bolsters the secondary depth, which matters mainly for IDP.
signals.quote: He's healthy back to himself. So he'll be up ready to go this Sunday.

signals.claim: The Texans' run game depends on sustaining blocks better against interior pressure such as Jeffery Simmons.
signals.note: Montgomery has been hit in the backfield often; the Titans' interior defensive line is a risk to his efficiency.
signals.quote: For us to improve in the running game, we have to sustain our blocks better.

signals.claim: Pass protection has improved and Stroud is throwing the ball well.
signals.note: Stable protection supports the passing game, which is where the offense is currently stronger than its run game.
signals.quote: CJ is throwing the ball well.

topics.detail: Ryans is taking over defensive play-calling from Matt Burke to fix communication and spark change after four games. He stressed it is not an overhaul and no slight against Burke.

Ryans said turnovers come in bunches and the team keeps attacking the ball, citing three passes where the ball went up and was completed. He expects the defense to get back to its aggressive style, with a safety playing center field.
The offensive line's mentality is fine, Ryans said, but it needs to finish and stay attached to blocks in the run game. Jeffery Simmons (No. 98) is the primary challenge.
Ryans praised Tennessee's quarterback, running backs, defense and special teams. He said he and Saleh are close friends going back to 2006 and called the game a must-win for both teams.

title: Jim Harbaugh on the Rookie Offensive Linemen Stepping Up
headline: Chargers' offensive line is thin: Slater, Alt and Penning reportedly aren't practicing, and rookie linemen are in elevated roles. Brenen Thompson and Ladd McConkey are on the field with unclear workloads, and Charlie Kolar is back at practice.
summary: Harbaugh opened with a list of players who won't practice, apparently Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, Trevor Penning, Derwin James, Donte Jackson and Khalil Mack (a rest day), plus one name the captions garbled. Brenen Thompson and Ladd McConkey will be on the field, but he wasn't sure how much they would do, and a full report would follow after practice. Asked whether an injury was day to day or week to week, he said only that the player is 'working through something', without naming him. Charlie Kolar, who had surgery about two weeks ago, did some work last week and is back out there. Scott Matlock and Branson Taylor are also back, and newly added Daniel Brunskill was praised for his versatility and familiarity with the scheme. Harbaugh praised the rookie offensive linemen for their demeanor and focus after they played this past weekend. He said Travis Burke handled a stretch of playing tight end and then shifting back to tackle, and that he can now focus solely on tackle this week. On Denver, he called Bo Nix elusive and special, and praised the Broncos' defense for mixing man, zone and match coverage and for an excellent pass rush.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said confidence is earned, not given, and praised the rookies' focus and demeanor after they played in the game this past weekend. He said they 'acquitted themselves well.'
Harbaugh has a lot of respect for the Broncos' coach and said the defense will play man, zone and match coverage. He called the pass rush and defensive line excellent, well coordinated and talented.
Harbaugh praised Nix's elite dodging and slipperiness, his ability to get out of the pocket and make plays, and called him special.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 7, 2026
headline: Lane Johnson retires and rookie Markel Bell steps in at right tackle; Dameon Pierce is elevated as the lead back with Tank Bigsby down, in an offense missing roughly six starters.
summary: Sirianni opened by saying he loves Lane Johnson and will miss him, and that he is excited about Markel Bell's chance to grow in the starting role after handling last week's circumstances well. He said the team reset today by reviewing the keys to winning, staying together and locking arms during a two-game losing streak (2-2 overall). Asked about the O-line, he said there is no secret to building cohesion with so many moving pieces: it takes walk-through reps, practice reps and meeting time. On the offense missing about six starters and key backups, he called it life in the NFL, said he will not use it as an excuse, and said he has to balance keeping players healthy against enough practice work. He said the 83 defensive snaps are best managed by the offense staying on the field and finishing drives, and that Wednesday's practice would be different to manage health. He said he still has conviction in the offense, pointing to the 2024 adjustments that led to a run of success. On the backfield, he praised Dameon Pierce as an NFL starting-caliber back who ran well in the preseason and said he is excited for his opportunity with Tank Bigsby down. He gave no specifics on snap shares or a depth chart.

injuries.detail: Sirianni said Bigsby is 'down right now'; no diagnosis or timeline given, and Pierce was elevated to the active roster in his place.
Retired; he will not play the rest of the season.

signals.claim: Will be the starting right tackle, replacing the retired Lane Johnson.
signals.note: A rookie replacing an elite tackle could mean more pass-protection risk for Hurts and the Eagles' skill players.
signals.quote: I'm really excited for markel's opportunity.

signals.claim: Will step into the lead running back role while Tank Bigsby is out.
signals.note: Pierce is the likely lead back with Bigsby down, though the coach did not detail his workload or how the carries will be split.
signals.quote: He's an NFL starting running back that was on our practice squad

signals.claim: Bigsby is unavailable at present, so his carries go to others.
signals.note: His absence opens the backfield work for Pierce and possibly others.
signals.quote: with tank being down right now

signals.claim: Johnson's retirement takes him off the roster for the rest of the year.
signals.note: Losing an elite right tackle weakens the offensive line for the whole offense.
signals.quote: I'll miss him dearly.

topics.detail: The line is unsettled, with Bell starting at right tackle, a possible different left guard depending on the protocol situation, and Sirianni stressing practice and meeting time to build cohesion.
At 2-2 and on a two-game losing streak, Sirianni stressed unity, not making excuses and not blaming individuals, and said the team has handled a similar stretch before in 2024.
The defense played 83 snaps in the loss and tired late. Sirianni said the fix is for the offense to finish drives and stay on the field, and that the team manages the load during the week.
The heavy offensive line package was used near the goal line because of the trust the coaches have in those players; no names were given.
